# galaxy_live_table (Resource)





<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `failure_mode` (String) Failure mode
- `schema_name` (String) Name of the table's schema
- `table_name` (String) Table name
- `type_properties` (Attributes) Type-specific properties for the new live table (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--type_properties))

### Optional

- `catalog_id` (String) ID of the table publisher catalog, a Glue or Galaxy metastore catalog. Optional when galaxyRestCatalogId is set
- `data_retention_days` (Number) If configured, data older than dataRetentionDays is deleted from Iceberg; otherwise, data is kept forever
- `description` (String) Table description
- `galaxy_rest_catalog_id` (String) ID of the Galaxy REST metastore catalog serving the table. Optional when catalogId is set. When both are set the catalogs must share the same default bucket and directory, and the table publisher catalog's storage settings apply
- `snapshot_retention_days` (Number) Number of days to retain table snapshots; older snapshots are automatically removed during maintenance

### Read-Only

- `catalog_name` (String) Name of the catalog supplying the table's storage location: the table publisher catalog if set, otherwise the Galaxy REST metastore catalog
- `cloud_region_id` (String) Region in which the table is stored
- `error_notification_count` (Number) Number of undismissed error notifications in the last five days
- `id` (String) Terraform import identifier.
- `live_table_id` (String) Table ID
- `live_table_state` (String) Table state
- `stop_message` (String) Message explaining why the table was stopped
- `stop_type` (String) Type of stop event if table is stopped
- `warn_notification_count` (Number) Number of undismissed warning notifications in the last five days

<a id="nestedatt--type_properties"></a>
### Nested Schema for `type_properties`

Required:

- `type_key` (String)

Optional:

- `columns` (Attributes List) Output columns of the transform; each carries its name, type, and the Trino SQL scalar expression over the input table's columns that produces its value (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--type_properties--columns))
- `csv_parameters` (Attributes) CSV format parameters. Required for CSV format, must be absent for other formats (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--type_properties--csv_parameters))
- `fanout_columns` (Attributes List) Fans the table's output out into one sink table per distinct combination of these column values, instead of a single output table. Order is part of the route's identity, and the columns cannot be changed once the table exists (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--type_properties--fanout_columns))
- `file_format` (String) File format
- `file_ingest_source_id` (String) ID of the file ingest source obtained from the /fileIngestSource endpoint
- `filter_expressions` (List of String) Trino SQL boolean predicates over the input table's columns that select which rows are emitted; at most one is supported
- `kafka_ingest_source_id` (String) ID of the Kafka ingest source obtained from the /kafkaIngestSource endpoint
- `kafka_topic_name` (String) Kafka topic name
- `latency_mode` (String) Latency mode for commits
- `live_table_id` (String) ID of the source table
- `partition_max_bytes_per_sec` (Number) Throughput limit per partition
- `path_suffix` (String) Suffix to append to the name from ingest source
- `polling_interval_in_minutes` (Number) List files in object storage every polling interval
- `schema_registry_id` (String) Schema registry ID associated with the live table
- `sort_column_name` (String) Sort column
- `start_strategy` (String) Stream start strategy
- `subject_name` (String) Subject name in the schema registry
- `user_defined_partition_spec` (Attributes List) Custom partition spec for transform live tables (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--type_properties--user_defined_partition_spec))
- `user_defined_schema` (Attributes List) Schema of the transformed table (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--type_properties--user_defined_schema))

<a id="nestedatt--type_properties--columns"></a>
### Nested Schema for `type_properties.columns`

Required:

- `expression` (String) Trino SQL scalar expression over the input table's columns that produces this column's value
- `name` (String) Name of the output column; adheres to Trino conventions
- `type` (Attributes) Column type; adheres to Trino conventions (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--type_properties--columns--type))

Optional:

- `nested_columns` (Attributes List) Nested columns for complex types (Row, Map, Array).
For primitive types, this list is empty.
For the Row type, this contains the fields of the row.
For the Map type, this contains the key and value types.
For the Array type, this contains the single element type. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--type_properties--columns--nested_columns))

Read-Only:

- `column_id` (Number) ID of the transform column
- `trino_column_name` (String) Column name
- `trino_type` (Attributes) Column type; adheres to Trino conventions (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--type_properties--columns--trino_type))

<a id="nestedatt--type_properties--columns--type"></a>
### Nested Schema for `type_properties.columns.type`

Required:

- `type_id` (String) Trino type enum

Optional:

- `type_parameters` (Map of String) Parameters for completing the type specification.
Types Decimal, Time, Timestamp, and TimestampTz require a parameter named `precision`, which is the number of digits.
Type Decimal also requires a parameter named `scale`, which is the number of digits to the right of the decimal point.


<a id="nestedatt--type_properties--columns--nested_columns"></a>
### Nested Schema for `type_properties.columns.nested_columns`

Required:

- `name` (String) Name of the nested field; adheres to Trino conventions
- `type` (Attributes) Column type; adheres to Trino conventions (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--type_properties--columns--nested_columns--type))

Optional:

- `nested_columns` (String) Nested columns for complex types (Row, Map, Array).
For primitive types, this list is empty.
For the Row type, this contains the fields of the row.
For the Map type, this contains the key and value types.
For the Array type, this contains the single element type.

Encoded as a JSON string because this type is recursive.

Optional:

- `bucket_count` (Number) Bucket count when transformType=bucket
- `truncate_width` (Number) Width when transformType=truncate


<a id="nestedatt--type_properties--user_defined_schema"></a>
### Nested Schema for `type_properties.user_defined_schema`

Required:

- `field_parser_config` (Attributes) JSON pointer (and parsing parameters) to the raw-table field transformed into this column value (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--type_properties--user_defined_schema--field_parser_config))
- `trino_column_name` (String) Name of the transform column; adheres to Trino conventions
- `trino_type` (Attributes) Column type; adheres to Trino conventions (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--type_properties--user_defined_schema--trino_type))

Optional:

- `nested_columns` (Attributes List) Nested columns for complex types (Row, Map, Array).
For primitive types, this list is empty.
For the Row type, this contains the fields of the row.
For the Map type, this contains the key and value types.
For the Array type, this contains the single element type. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--type_properties--user_defined_schema--nested_columns))

Read-Only:

- `column_id` (Number) ID of the transform column

<a id="nestedatt--type_properties--user_defined_schema--field_parser_config"></a>
### Nested Schema for `type_properties.user_defined_schema.field_parser_config`

Required:

- `pointer` (String) JSON pointer (IETF RFC 6901)

Optional:

- `parse_parameters` (Map of String) Parameters for parsing Varchar and time types.
For Varchar, the only allowed parameter is "varchar.type", with valid values "scalar" or "json".
For Timestamp and TimestampTz, the only allowed parameters are:
  - "timestamp.converter", with valid values "unixtime" or "iso8601".
  - "timestamp.unit", with valid values "nanos", "micros", "millis", "secs", "mins", "hours", or "days".
